First, we complete a truth table for the part in the inner-most parentheses, $A∧B.$ The statement $A∧B$ is true if both $A$ and $B$ are true.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Next, we look at the columns labeled $A$ and $A∧B$ to complete a truth table for the part in the parentheses, $(A∧B)∨A.$ The statement $(A∧B)∨A$ is true if either $A∧B$ is true, $A$ is true, or both $A∧B$ and $A$ are true.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ | $\,(A∧B)∨A\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Finally, we look at the columns labeled $B$ and $(A∧B)∨A$ to complete the column $((A∧B)∨A)∧B.$ The statement $((A∧B)∨A)∧B$ is true if both $(A∧B)∨A$ and $B$ are true.

The completed truth table is shown below:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ | $\,(A∧B)∨A\,$ | $\,((A∧B)∨A)∧B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
